strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-7 points

Overview: Buy one, get three free! Oricorio provides cheap and flexible role compression through its four different formes, entry hazard control, pivoting, and even disruption. Offensively, it's no slouch either, having access to the coveted Quiver Dance alongside Terastallization, with Revelation Dance acting as a stronger Tera Blast. Despite these boons, Oricorio remains held back by its poor stats and common weaknesses, particularly to Rock, which is not only shared amongst formes but also often forces it to rely on Heavy-Duty Boots to perform its roles.

Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: Oricorio can take advantage of Quiver Dance to set up and sweep opposing teams. Often, this leverages Terastallization defensively to give an opening to use Quiver Dance safely or offensively to give Revelation Dance a new typing. It is also worth noting that Dancer lets it mirror opposing dance moves, giving it an immediate power boost if it switches in on one.

Defensive Pivot: Thanks to its four different typings, Oricorio can tailor itself to check specific Pokemon. It can take hits and threaten back with STAB moves, pivot out with U-turn, stop setup and entry hazards with Taunt, or even remove hazards with Defog. This set needs heavy defensive investment alongside Roost and often Heavy-Duty Boots to enable it to come in multiple times over the course of a game. Note that Oricorio-G can also act as a spinblocker by virtue of its Ghost type.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Revelation Dance, Hurricane, Air Slash

Setup Moves: Quiver Dance

Utility Moves: Defog, U-turn, Taunt, Roost, Substitute

Coverage: Alluring Voice, Icy Wind

Niche Moves

Tailwind: The combination of Tailwind and U-turn lets Oricorio provide speed control to its teammates. Oricorio can also use it offensively to outspeed foes and fire off an attack.

Charm / Feather Dance: Oricorio can weaken opposing attacks to check threats it could not normally handle, keeping itself healthy afterwards with Roost or using U-turn on the forced switch to gain momentum.

Physical Attacks: In some matchups, Oricorio can look to copy a Swords Dance or Dragon Dance boost to turn the tables on opposing setup sweepers. In these cases, it can opt for Acrobatics or Dual Wingbeat to attempt to return some damage. Note that using Acrobatics comes with the additional expense of being itemless or running an item other than Heavy-Duty Boots, which is normally vital. Oricorio can also use Swords Dance itself to boost its Attack, but this is not recommended due to Oricorio's inherent lack of damage and Speed.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots is Oricorio's go-to item. Nullifying its weakness to Stealth Rock allows Oricorio to reliably perform its role while lowering its dependence on Roost to stay healthy.

Niche Items

Rocky Helmet: With three formes sporting a resistance to Bug, a Rocky Helmet can punish U-turn spam or simply wear down physical attackers through Oricorio's repeated use of Roost to shrug off attacks.

Leftovers: In cases where the opposing team has weak entry hazard setters, the passive recovery from Leftovers lowers Oricorio's reliance on Roost, allowing it to better defensively check some Pokemon.

Choice Scarf: A Choice Scarf lets Oricorio function as a revenge killer while retaining its ability to pivot.

Damage-boosting Items: On setup sweeper sets, Oricorio might appreciate the extra boost to its damage provided by items like Life Orb and Expert Belt, at the potential cost of longevity or setup opportunities from lacking Heavy-Duty Boots.

Tera

Oricorio can effectively leverage Terastallization to make up for its mediocre stats, common weaknesses, and lack of coverage. It can be easily slotted onto teams as a cheap secondary Tera Captain. Defensively, Oricorio can run Rock-resistant Tera types, such as Tera Steel and Ground, to remove its Stealth Rock weakness. Other defensive Tera types such as Tera Grass and Water can be used to improve its defensive typing by getting around its weaknesses. Offensively, you can tailor Oricorio to overcome its checks by changing the type of its signature Revelation Dance, such as using Tera Ground on Oricorio-E to beat Electric-types or Tera Fairy on Oricorio-G to get around Dark-types. Be careful with when you decide to Tera Oricorio, as you give up the ability to Terastallize your stronger Tera Captain, in addition to losing Oricorio's original STAB type on Revelation Dance, as the type of the move changes to match its new type.

Draft Strategy

Oricorio is ultimately a cheap role compression Pokemon, so it should never be drafted around. Even still, its flexibility as a pivot, utility as extra hazard control, and capability as a secondary Tera Captain means it can be effectively used on most drafts.

Entry Hazard Removal: Given the scarcity of entry hazard removal, Oricorio's access to Defog can free up a moveslot on your primary hazard remover for it to fulfill a different role. Having hazard removal elsewhere similarly opens up Oricorio to run its niche items or moves such as Taunt. Some examples are Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Quaquaval.

Fighting- and Ground-weak Pokemon: Oricorio's immunity or resistance to both types allows it to come in on STAB attacks from Fighting- and Ground-types and offensively threaten them back with Flying-type STAB moves or gain momentum through U-turn. Examples of Fighting- and Ground-weak Pokemon it can support include Darkrai, Iron Hands, and Iron Moth.

Wallbreakers: Since Oricorio wants to either pivot or set up a Quiver Dance, strong wallbreakers enable and are enabled by it. Ground-type wallbreakers like Garchomp and both Ursaluna formes are especially useful, as they can come in on the Rock- and Electric-type moves that Oricorio often fears.

Checks and Counters

Rock- and Electric-types: Oricorio struggles to deal damage to and is forced out by Rock- and Electric-type Pokemon. Its lackluster defensive stats even after investment mean that most STAB moves from these foes will easily 2HKO or OHKO Oricorio (barring Oricorio-E, which is not weak to Electric-type moves).

Knock Off: Much of Oricorio's effectiveness can be attributed to its item of choice, so removing that item greatly impairs its ability to perform its role. This is especially a problem for Oricorio-P and Oricorio-G, which are naturally weak to Knock Off as well.

Strong Offensive Pokemon: Bulky or faster offensive Pokemon that can hit Oricorio even neutrally are able to power through its weak defensive stats, neutralizing its effectiveness or forcing it to switch out.

Disruption: If running a setup sweeper set, disruption moves such as Taunt, Encore, and Trick can halt Oricorio's movement by preventing or limiting the effectiveness of Quiver Dance. Prankster Pokemon with access to these moves, like Grimmsnarl and Whimsicott, are especially worth mention, as Oricorio cannot prevent their moves from going off with its own Taunt.
